 Volkswagen announces recall for 5,000 EVs over overheating risk
 By
 Ryan Gilmore 
 |
 9 November 2026
 News
 Recalls 
 Always stay up-to-date with Recalls direct to your inbox
 Sign up to the newsletter 
 Volkswagen has announced a recall for examples from five of its ID range of EVs, as well as certain Cupra Born models over concerns that the battery fitted may overheat and pose a fire risk.  
 Volkswagen has announced that certain models of the ID Buzz , ID 3, ID 4, ID 5 and ID 7 built between 2022 and 2025 are part of the recall and that the issue related to components within the high-voltage batteries. It’s understood that this recall affects roughly 5,000 cars in the UK while 85,000 cars globally have been affected.  
 An over-the-air (OTA) update to recalled models has already been applied and will temporarily limit the maximum charge to 80% as a safety precaution, although the cars will remain safe to drive. The mandatory OTA update has raised questions from fleet operators on the impact this could have for operations and is part of a wider conversation on OTA updates reducing a vehicle's capabilities . 
 Ensure you always get Fleet News insight. Make us your preferred source on Google 
 Volkswagen said it had communicated with retail customers for whom it held contact details, added information to relevant brand websites and is working with fleet companies to notify them in advance of the recall and temporary charging restrictions.
 Volkswagen also confirmed that the charging restriction would be lifted once the recalled car had been inspected. For models that don’t meet the quality standards, a software-based solution will be applied.     
 Only Volkswagen and Cupra affected so far
 All the cars recalled so far sit on Volkswagen’s MEB platform, a platform that also underpins popular Audi models (including the Q4 e-tron ), Ford (Explorer and Capri) and Skoda models ( Enyaq and Elroq). No recalls have been announced for these models as of yet.

 Author:
 Ryan Gilmore 
 Content editor 
 ryan.gilmore@bauermedia.co.uk 
 Ryan joined Fleet News as a content editor in 2026.
 In his role, he is primarily responsible for working alongside manufacturers to create engaging bespoke content. Ryan also helps promote Fleet News events and has hosted panel discussions at Fleet & Mobility Live.
 Beyond that, Ryan is also a seasoned road tester, news writer and has interviewed top industry figures on everything from future models to alternative fuel strategies.  
 Prior to joining Fleet News, Ryan spent five years working for Parkers.co.uk , and for two-years he was the car buying editor where he managed all the leasing and used car content.
 He also holds a BA in Politics from the University of Hull as well as an MA in Automotive Journalism from Coventry University.
 He says: “The new car market has never been trickier to navigate with challenger brands, different fuel types and changing legislation all making future planning difficult. I enjoy working with manufacturers to see how their models can cut through the noise and resonate with fleet decision makers.”
